title: Declining performance of master athletes: silhouettes of the trajectory of healthy human ageing?
population: Review of world-record performances of master athletes and a proposed set-point theory
findings: World-record analysis suggests an essentially linear performance decline with age until about the eighth decade, after which decline accelerates.
Because records come from highly trained individuals, the authors argue they reflect the diminution of integrative physiology due to ageing alone, unconfounded by inactivity.

The authors propose a set-point theory: a threshold of physical activity is needed to age optimally; exercising below it results in ageing contaminated by the effects of inactivity, while exercise above it stimulates adaptations to maximise athletic performance.
They argue the controlled decades-long decline in athletic performance should not be seen as a disease process.
limitations: Hypothesis-generating review built on world-record data from different individuals (the limitation Lepers 2021 and Stones 2019 stress); set-point theory is untested.
implications: A near-linear decline to about age 70 followed by acceleration is a defensible default curve shape for elite-level performance, consistent with Ganse 2020's steeper post-70 decline.
Recommend a minimum-consistency framing: reduced training volume or frequency adds decline beyond the ageing trajectory.
